title: Underwriting Guideline — The Underlying Primary Policy and the Attachment Points of Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)
content:
## 1. One live policy per address

Only one Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines) policy may be live on a property address: a new policy is bound only when no other Excess Flood policy at the same property address is in status pending effective or active. This is read from Tidemark's own policy records for that property address before the policy is bound; a policy at the same address that has expired or been cancelled does not stand in the way.

## 2. The underlying primary policy

An Excess Flood policy always sits over a primary flood policy on the same home of a kind the tier accepts. A policy is bound or renewed only when declarations of the underlying primary flood policy showing it in force on the excess term start are on file; when the underlying is a Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form or HomeFlood policy, the Tidemark policy record itself is that evidence. The evidence is Tidemark's record of the declarations received (or of the Tidemark primary policy), matched to the underlying policy number the excess policy is bound over, and it must be on file before the binding or renewal is made.

## 3. Attachment points

The attachment points are fixed at binding from the underlying type:

| Underlying policy | Building attachment point | Contents attachment point |
|---|---|---|
| NFIP Dwelling Form policy | the tier's dwelling attachment point over an NFIP Dwelling Form policy | the tier's personal property attachment point over an NFIP Dwelling Form policy |
| Private primary flood policy | the underlying dwelling limit, but never less than the tier's lowest dwelling attachment point over a private primary policy | the underlying personal property limit, but never less than the tier's lowest personal property attachment point over a private primary policy |

Worked illustration (hypothetical figures): over a private primary policy with an underlying dwelling limit of 400000 and a personal property limit of 60000, on a tier whose private-primary floors are 250000 and 100000, the building attachment point is the higher of 400000 and 250000, that is 400000, and the contents attachment point is the higher of 60000 and 100000, that is 100000.

## 4. No drop-down

When the tier does not provide drop-down on an underlying gap, the excess policy never pays any part of a loss below its attachment point — not when the underlying policy has lapsed, been cancelled or carries a lower limit, and not when the underlying carrier pays less for its own deductible or exclusions; the insured bears that gap.
